clue.text: Quickly deposit balance in post office

indicators.note: to deposit something is to lodge it inside somewhere, so one piece is placed within another
in says where the deposited piece goes: within the post office letters

parts.note: the balance is the rest, what remains

explanation.surface: Instructions to pay in the rest of one's money at the post office without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction meaning very fast, hence quickly in general use.

clue.text: For and against stopping unfeigned censure

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these pieces sit inside the other

parts.note: unfeigned means genuine, real
pro means for, in favour of
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Weighing arguments for and against before delivering a sincere rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproval is a rebuke or scolding, the same thing as a censure.

clue.text: Spy captured by Poles extremely sick in Russian city

indicators.note: captured by means held between, so the spy goes inside the pair of poles

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A Cold War tale of an agent seized by Polish forces while gravely ill in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people, but it is the two compass points S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Smolensk is a city in western Russia on the Dnieper.

clue.text: Smile upon frolics without forethought

indicators.note: frolics suggests letters romping about, so the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grin breaks out and someone capers about, quite spontaneously.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse means acting suddenly and without planning, with no forethought.

clue.text: Salesman coming back to get empty case willy-nilly

indicators.note: coming back means the salesman word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
for can mean to get, as in sending for a doctor

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A travelling rep returns to collect an empty suitcase whether he likes it or not.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce means by necessity, unavoidably, much as willy-nilly does.

clue.text: Informed cast

definitions.meaning: informed means brought up to date, told what is happening
cast means given a role in a film or picture

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to brief someone; read literally it means placing an actor in a film.

clue.text: Islanders see bats after game

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the game in the answer

parts.note: faro is an old gambling card game

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters of see are scrambled

explanation.surface: People from an island watch the bats come out after a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faroese are the people of the Faroe Islands in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: French tragedian's singular piquancy

parts.note: Jean Racine was a French writer of tragedies in the 17th century
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Praise for the unique sharpness of a French playwright's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Raciness means a lively, spicy quality, the same as piquancy.

clue.text: A Danish port relies on winds

indicators.note: winds means twists about, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Danish harbour that depends on the wind for its shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsinore (Helsingor) is the port where Hamlet is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the English name of Helsingor, a Danish port town on the Oresund.

clue.text: One making pithy observations in past about boundaries of parish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the past tense goes round the other letters

parts.note: the aorist is a past tense in Greek grammar

indicators.note: boundaries of points to the outer letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A local wit who once wandered the edges of the parish making sharp remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: AORIST is the Greek simple past tense, a term solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorist is a writer or speaker of aphorisms, short pithy sayings.

clue.text: Cat heard in ruins

indicators.note: heard means the clue is about a word as spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: the Rex is a breed of cat with curly fur

explanation.surface: A cat's cry can be heard among the ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecks are ruined remains, so the plural noun matches ruins.

clue.text: Find the writer filling in voucher

indicators.note: filling in means occupying the inside, so one piece goes into the voucher

parts.note: a coupon is a voucher
the writer is the setter, referring to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A setter discovers they are the one completing a discount voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something is to happen across it, to find it by chance.

clue.text: Standard writer with no name

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author who goes unnamed, presented as the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, which is a kind of standard.

clue.text: Marshal is held up in compound

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so the letters of the three words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawman is pinned down inside a fortified enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a sheriff's title, but here it is a verb, meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulphide is a chemical compound of sulphur with another element.

clue.text: Literary family with minimal amount of information to contribute

parts.note: the Doones are the outlaw family in Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
a bit, a binary digit, is the smallest unit of information

explanation.surface: A family of fiction each chipping in the smallest scrap of news.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's bit is to play one's part, making a contribution.

clue.text: Brickbats in part of lake

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Missiles thrown at someone in one section of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is severe criticism, and brickbats are critical remarks.

clue.text: Sucre, oft translated as sugar

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Spanish-sounding Sucre is often rendered in English as sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucre' is French for sugar, which invites translating it; instead its letters, with OFT, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fructose is fruit sugar, a simple sugar found in honey and fruit.

clue.text: Tack carried by a lean mountaineer

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the tack goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does
a pin is a tack, a small fastener

explanation.surface: A climber with thin build carrying tacks to fix the route.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a climber of high mountains, especially in the Alps.

clue.text: Current bishop's office that is now clear

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
a see is the diocese or office of a bishop

explanation.surface: The present bishop's office has just become clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what one says on understanding something that has been explained.

clue.text: Lady Chatterley has one for company, for example

indicators.note: has introduces the substitute that the lady's name takes on
for means in place of, so one piece replaces the other

parts.note: Constance is Lady Chatterley's first name in D H Lawrence's novel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Lady Chatterley takes a lover to keep her company, to give an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to her affair in Lady Chatterley's Lover; 'one for company' really swaps I in for CO.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example, a single case illustrating something.

clue.text: About time side finally put ball in net — so you'll never walk alone

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
about means surrounding, so the scoring word goes round the time letter

parts.note: to put the ball in the net is to have scored

explanation.surface: A football match report about a late goal, ending with the Liverpool anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: You'll Never Walk Alone is the anthem of Liverpool football fans; being escorted means someone walks beside you.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are accompanied by a companion you never walk on your own.

clue.text: Intense blue, despite appearances

parts.note: deep means intense, as of a colour or feeling
blue means sad, down in spirits

explanation.surface: A rich dark blue that is not what it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intense blue' reads as a shade of colour, but blue here means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in reality, at heart, whatever surface impressions suggest.

clue.text: Notices posted in a river and a large salt lake

indicators.note: posted in means placed inside, as notices are put up within something

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
ads are notices, advertisements

explanation.surface: Signs put up along a river and beside a vast saline lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea, between Israel and Jordan, is a large inland lake of very salty water.

clue.text: Object placed in receptacle for reptile

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the object goes within the receptacle

parts.note: a can is a container
an aim is an object, a goal

explanation.surface: Something put into a container intended for a pet reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The caiman is a Central and South American reptile related to alligators.

clue.text: Act of God? Conservative comes forward in response

indicators.note: comes forward means the letter moves towards the front of the word

parts.note: a reaction is a response

explanation.surface: A Tory steps up to reply to a question about divine acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation, the making of the world, is the supreme divine act in Genesis.

clue.text: Bird that's no good — holding it back is pointless

indicators.note: holding means enclosing, so the bird goes round the other piece
no good means the letter G, for good, is removed

parts.note: a goose is a bird

indicators.note: back means the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A useless bird that holds something back is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, futile and so pointless.

clue.text: Sophistication of one absorbing what's central in Cambridge degree

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the oneness word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: unity means oneness, being one

indicators.note: what's central in points to the middle letter of the word that follows

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Polish of a graduate soaking up the heart of a Cambridge education.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbanity means refined, courteous manners, a polished sophistication.

clue.text: Canteen in a mess concealing right way in

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece
in a mess means jumbled up, so the letters of the canteen word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A messy army canteen hides the proper route in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' turns CANTEEN into ENTANCE, and 'concealing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a door or opening, a way in.

clue.text: Hot tip in essay

indicators.note: in means inside, so the tip goes within the essay word

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try
a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A useful hint tucked into a written essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot in the sense of fashionable and popular, as in the latest craze.
